evals.prompt: How should I model a Product, a Review, and a Rating in an e-commerce domain? A Product has a name, description, price, and category. A Review has a text body and belongs to one Product and one User. A Rating is a score from 1-5 associated with a Review.
evals.expected_output: Intent is 'how should I model' → load reference.md directly and guide through building block classification. Product: Entity (unique identity, has lifecycle). Review: Entity if reviews have individual identity (can be edited/deleted). Rating: Value Object (no identity of its own, defined entirely by its score 1-5, immutable). Category: Value Object (enumerable, no identity). Price: Value Object (amount + currency, immutable). Aggregate boundaries: Product is its own Aggregate root; Review is its own Aggregate (do not nest Reviews inside Product — that creates a large Aggregate). Reviews reference Product by ID only (never hold object reference). Must explain the Value Object vs Entity distinction using the identity test.
assertions: Loads reference.md for modeling guidance
Classifies Product as Entity
Classifies Rating as Value Object with explanation (no identity, defined by value)
Classifies Price as Value Object
Recommends separate Aggregates for Product and Review
States Reviews reference Product by ID only
Explains Value Object vs Entity using identity test
